subject: Technical deep dive recap - latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: discovery + next steps

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the things we heard as your top priorities: 

- Primary pain: P99 latency spikes during peak inference for your chat assistant causing poor UX for premium customers.
- Traffic profile: relatively low baseline (200 qps) with frequent 10-15 minute burst windows up to ~1,200 qps.
- Model: evaluating open models (Llama-family variants), looking at ~70B scale for best quality with option to quantize.
- Constraints: strict VPC requirement, customer data must remain in your AWS account (no egress), and SOC 2 evidence required for procurement.

Goals we discussed:
- 95th percentile latency target: <= 150ms for 512-token generation on typical prompt distribution.
- Sustained throughput: 600 qps with headroom for burst scaling to 1.2k qps.
- Cost target: reduce current per-token spend by ~30% while maintaining output quality.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive session with our infra/serving team to validate SLO feasibility and deployment topology (cc'ing Laura to coordinate).
2) Share our SLO/template + rough topology diagram ahead of the session (attached).
3) Customer security questionnaire + SOC2 artifacts (we'll follow up via the security track).

I've attached a short SLO template and a draft topology diagram to help frame the deep-dive. Laura — can you propose 2x slots next week?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — this is perfect and captures the discussion. A couple clarifications before the deep-dive:

- We prefer a private deployment inside our AWS account (VPC peering) but are open to dedicated Redwood capacity if the economics work.
- For models: we want to evaluate both 70B and a tuned 13B fall-back for cost-sensitive flows.

I'll loop in our infra lead (infra@acme.ai) if that helps on the deep-dive call. Please include any kernel/quantization recommendations in the pre-read.

Date: 2027-05-13T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs + model requirements

Sanjay —

Appreciate the time yesterday. Below is the technical recap from our deep-dive with Marissa (serving/runtime) and Laura (solutions). This is meant to capture the asks and our initial feasibility notes so we can align on a proposed topology and concrete validation plan.

Pain points reiterated:
- Periodic burst traffic (10-15m) causes CPU/GPU queueing which spikes tail latency.
- Cache warming: cold starts for KV cache when routing across pods increase p99.
- Cost: large-model token cost is material; you're looking for a path to keep quality while reducing per-token spend.

SLOs / targets discussed:
- 95th percentile latency (512-token gen): <= 150ms (primary)
- P99 latency target: <= 300ms with graceful degradation/fallback
- Sustained throughput baseline: 600 qps with autoscale to 1.2k qps within 45s
- Availability: 99.9% regionally for production routes

Model requirements / execution profile:
- Primary model: Llama-70B (or equivalent) quantized to 4-bit where possible for cost efficiency. Prefer FP16 execution for engineering path if customers accept slightly higher memory requirements.
- Fall-back model: tuned 13B distilled variant for cost-sensitive routes and backups during peak.
- Streaming + KV cache support required for chat use case (low-latency prefix retrieval).
- Max context: 4k tokens (we'll validate token distributions from your logs).

Deployment topology options (feasibility notes):
1) Private deployment (customer VPC, Redwood control plane):
   - Pros: meets your data residency/VPC needs, direct peering, customer-owned infra.
   - Cons: requires infra ops for node provisioning; Redwood provides an on-prem package + deployment playbook.
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in us-west):
   - Pros: predictable throughput, autoscaling, managed fallbacks and rolling upgrades. Can meet 95th percentile SLO with appropriate batching and prefix caching.
   - Cons: needs secure connectivity to your data sources (we can set up private endpoints).
3) Hybrid: Primary dedicated for production routes + private for sensitive traffic. Multi-region fallback to eu-west for geo resilience.

Key risk areas and mitigation:
- Cold-start / cache warming: implement continuous KV cache warmers for hot keys and prefixed batching for common prompts. Measured improvement expected: 30-50% reduction in p99 tails.
- Quantization/regression: we'll run model-quality evals on a shared prompt set before enabling 4-bit quantized variant in prod.
- Autoscale time to scale: tune autoscale to pre-warm capacity based on predictable traffic signals and use short-lived burst pools for 45s windows.

Validation plan / next steps:
- Redwood to run a load validation in our staging environment that mirrors your burst profile (we'll need sample request traces).
- Shared eval: Marissa will run quality regression tests between 70B FP16, 4-bit quant, and 13B fallback on your prompt set.
- Deliverables: SLO template (attached), proposed topology diagram (attached), test plan and runbook.

Marissa — can you add estimated validation timelines and the quality/regression checklist? Laura — please propose 2x slots for the validation planning call.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs + model requirements

Thanks all — quick follow-up with estimated timelines and concrete next steps from the infra/validation side.

Estimated validation timeline (targeting 2 weeks):
- Day 0-2: ingest sample request traces and agree on traffic shape + test harness.
- Day 3-7: run model-quality evals (70B FP16 vs 4-bit quant vs 13B fallback) on supplied prompt set.
- Day 8-10: run load validation in staging with burst patterns (600 qps sustained, bursts to 1.2k qps).
- Day 11-14: analyze results, recommend final topology and quantization profile.

Deliverables we'll hand over:
- Quality/regression report (comparative metrics + example failures)
- Load validation report with latency percentiles per route/model variant
- Recommended production config: batch sizes, cache warmers, autoscale thresholds, and rollout plan

Action items:
- Sanjay: share 24-48h of anonymized request traces and a representative prompt set (secure upload/link).
- Aditya/Laura: coordinate a planning call for Monday 05/24 or Tuesday 05/25 (two 45-min options).
- Redwood: we'll publish the validation plan doc to the Drive link in the thread.

If we can get the traces by EOD Thu, we can start Day 0 Fri and aim to complete the validation window before the end of the month.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
